medfit's quality control checks the native engine against independent SEM software
([Quality control of the optimizer](quality-control.html)). This page writes the same simple
mediation model in each package's own syntax, so the comparisons can be read and rerun. The
lavaan and OpenMx blocks run when the site is built and stop the build if they drift from
medfit. The semopy block is Python: its script and its output are saved in the package
(`tests/sim/oracles/`), and the build checks the saved output against medfit.

The model: `treatment` affects `mediator1` (path `a`), `mediator1` affects `outcome` (path
`b`), and `treatment` affects `outcome` directly (path `cp`), on the bundled `mediation_demo`
data (n = 400).

| | medfit | lavaan | OpenMx | semopy 2.3.11 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Label a path | `mediator1 ~ a*treatment` | `mediator1 ~ a*treatment` | `mxPath(..., labels = "a")` | `mediator1 ~ a*treatment` |
| Indirect effect | `ab := a*b` | `ab := a*b` | `mxAlgebra(a * b, name = "ab")` | not in the syntax: `:=` is an unknown command; compute `a * b` from the estimates |
| Exogenous variance | estimated; `fixed_x = TRUE` fixes it | fixed by default; `fixed.x = FALSE` estimates it | estimated when you write its path | not estimated (no row in the output) |
| Tight convergence | default | default | `mxOption()` tolerances (defaults stop up to about 5.5e-6 away) | `options = {"ftol": 1e-12}` (the default stops about 4e-5 away) |

## medfit

```{r}
#| label: medfit
library(medfit)
library(generics)
model <- "
  mediator1 ~ a*treatment
  outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment
  ab := a*b
"
native <- tidy(fit_sem(model, mediation_demo))
native[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")]
```

## lavaan

```{r}
#| label: lavaan
library(lavaan)
lav <- parameterEstimates(sem(model, mediation_demo, fixed.x = FALSE))
lav[lav$label %in% c("a", "b", "cp", "ab"), c("label", "est", "se")]
```

The [lavaan comparison](lavaan-comparison.html) covers the rest of the overlap and where the
two differ by design.

## OpenMx

OpenMx describes the model as paths in a RAM model. The data are the sample covariance matrix
with `numObs` set to n, the maximum-likelihood fit medfit uses; `compare_lr()` builds its
OpenMx models the same way (from the raw data the fit used when the fit has a mean structure).

```{r}
#| label: openmx
library(OpenMx)
old <- c(mxOption(NULL, "Optimality tolerance"), mxOption(NULL, "Feasibility tolerance"),
         mxOption(NULL, "Function precision"))
mxOption(NULL, "Optimality tolerance", 1e-12)
mxOption(NULL, "Feasibility tolerance", 1e-12)
mxOption(NULL, "Function precision", 1e-15)
vars <- c("treatment", "mediator1", "outcome")
omx <- mxModel(
  "simple", type = "RAM", manifestVars = vars,
  mxPath(from = "treatment", to = "mediator1", labels = "a"),
  mxPath(from = "mediator1", to = "outcome", labels = "b"),
  mxPath(from = "treatment", to = "outcome", labels = "cp"),
  mxPath(from = vars, arrows = 2, values = 1, labels = c("v_x", "v_m", "v_y")),
  mxAlgebra(a * b, name = "ab"),
  mxData(observed = cov(mediation_demo[, vars]), type = "cov", numObs = nrow(mediation_demo))
)
omx <- mxRun(omx, silent = TRUE)
omx_est <- summary(omx)$parameters
omx_est[omx_est$name %in% c("a", "b", "cp"), c("name", "Estimate", "Std.Error")]
mxEval(ab, omx)
```

```{r}
#| label: openmx-check
#| include: false
mxOption(NULL, "Optimality tolerance", old[[1]])
mxOption(NULL, "Feasibility tolerance", old[[2]])
mxOption(NULL, "Function precision", old[[3]])
paths <- c("a", "b", "cp")
nat <- native[match(paths, native$term), ]
omx_rows <- omx_est[match(paths, omx_est$name), ]
lav_rows <- lav[match(paths, lav$label), ]
stopifnot(
  max(abs(nat$estimate - omx_rows$Estimate)) < 1e-5,
  max(abs(nat$std_error - omx_rows$Std.Error)) < 1e-5,
  max(abs(nat$estimate - lav_rows$est)) < 1e-5,
  abs(native$estimate[native$term == "ab"] - mxEval(ab, omx)[1, 1]) < 1e-5
)
```

## semopy (Python)

[semopy](https://pypi.org/project/semopy/) reads lavaan-style syntax. It is not one of
medfit's quality-control oracles yet; this is the script that would be one, saved as
`tests/sim/oracles/semopy-simple.py`:

```{r}
#| label: semopy-script
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
oracles <- file.path(normalizePath(file.path("..", ".."), mustWork = FALSE), "tests", "sim", "oracles")
cat("```python", readLines(file.path(oracles, "semopy-simple.py")), "```", sep = "\n")
```

Its output from semopy 2.3.11 (2026-10-24), saved as `tests/sim/oracles/semopy-simple.csv`,
next to medfit with `fixed_x = TRUE`, which matches semopy's treatment of the exogenous
variable:

```{r}
#| label: semopy-output
semopy <- read.csv(file.path(oracles, "semopy-simple.csv"))
labels <- c("mediator1~treatment" = "a", "outcome~mediator1" = "b", "outcome~treatment" = "cp")
key <- paste0(semopy$lhs, semopy$op, semopy$rhs)
semopy$term <- ifelse(key %in% names(labels), labels[key], key)
stopifnot(nrow(semopy) == 5)
fixed <- tidy(fit_sem(model, mediation_demo, fixed_x = TRUE))
both <- merge(semopy[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")],
              fixed[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")], by = "term",
              suffixes = c("_semopy", "_medfit"))
both
stopifnot(max(abs(both$estimate_semopy - both$estimate_medfit)) < 1e-5,
          max(abs(both$std_error_semopy - both$std_error_medfit)) < 1e-5)
```

With semopy's default stopping rule the same script gives `a` = 0.456039 instead of
0.455996, a gap of about 4e-5, which is why the script sets `ftol`. Comparing software at 1e-6
means first checking that each one has actually converged.
